The logarithmic abundance notation is  

[X/Y] = log10[(nX/nY)star / (nX/nY)☉]

1. Star 1  
   • [Fe/H]₁ = 0 ⇒ (nFe/nH)₁ = (nFe/nH)☉  
   • [Si/Fe]₁ = 0.3 ⇒ (nSi/nFe)₁ = 10^0.3 · (nSi/nFe)☉  

   Therefore  
   (nSi/nH)₁ = (nSi/nFe)₁ · (nFe/nH)₁  
             = 10^0.3 · (nSi/nFe)☉ · (nFe/nH)☉  
             = 10^0.3 · (nSi/nH)☉.          …(1)

2. Star 2  
   • [Mg/H]₂ = 0 ⇒ (nMg/nH)₂ = (nMg/nH)☉  
   • [Mg/Si]₂ = 0.3 ⇒ (nMg/nSi)₂ = 10^0.3 · (nMg/nSi)☉  

   Rearranging gives (nSi/nMg)₂ = 1/[10^0.3 · (nMg/nSi)☉].  
   Hence  
   (nSi/nH)₂ = (nSi/nMg)₂ · (nMg/nH)₂  
             = [1/(10^0.3 · (nMg/nSi)☉)] · (nMg/nH)☉  
             = (1/10^0.3) · (nSi/nH)☉.          …(2)

3. Ratio of silicon atoms (per hydrogen)  

   (nSi/nH)₁ / (nSi/nH)₂ = [10^0.3 · (nSi/nH)☉] / [(1/10^0.3) · (nSi/nH)☉]  
                         = 10^{0.3 + 0.3}  
                         = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98.

Thus Star 1 has about 4 times as many silicon atoms in its photosphere (per H atom) as Star 2.
